# Spec: the Graphic dialog (phase 1 of 2 — browse, preview, insert; `.fjgraphic` export is phase 2)

## Goal
Insert ▸ Graphic… opens a sheet with categories | graphics | a looping preview, From File… at the bottom left and Cancel / Insert at the right, replacing the Insert ▸ Graphic submenu; every bundled template declares `meta.category` and `meta.description`. Agents get `list_graphics` and `insert_graphic`, the dialog's two acts.

## Files
- `graphic/tests/graphics/*.js` (all 23) — add `category` and a one-line `description` to `meta`; no other byte changes.
- `graphic/tests/template_meta.rs` (new) — every template's `meta.category` equals G-45 (c)'s table, `description` is a non-empty one-line string ≤ 120 chars.
- `graphic/CLAUDE.md` — the templates rule names G-45 and `template_meta.rs`.
- `docs/graphics-api.md`, `docs/graphics-api.d.ts` — `Meta` gains `category?` and `description?` (what the dialog does with each).
- `app/Sources/GraphicCatalog.swift` (new) — `GraphicBrowserItem`, `GraphicBrowserCategory`, `GraphicCatalog`, `GraphicTemplateLibrary`.
- `app/Sources/GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift` (new) — the sheet.
- `app/Sources/GraphicPreviewPlayer.swift` (new) — the off-main preview loop.
- `app/Sources/ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift` (new) — the insert bodies both doors share.
- `app/Sources/EditorViewController+GraphicMenus.swift` — `showGraphicBrowser(_:)` replaces `insertGraphicTemplate(_:)`; `insertGraphicFromFile` stops being a menu action (the sheet's From File… calls it); `insertGraphic(from:grouped:)` delegates to the document bodies; add `insertProjectGraphic(named:grouped:)`; validator arms.
- `app/Sources/EditorViewController+AddClips.swift` — extract `addGeneratedClip`'s track choice into `static generatedClipOps` (behaviour unchanged).
- `app/Sources/AppDelegate+GraphicMenu.swift` — Insert holds Adjustment Clip, then one item "Graphic…"; `graphicMenu()` removed; header comment rewritten.
- `app/Sources/GraphicTemplates.swift` — header comment (titles now come from `meta.name`; `title(for:)` is the fallback); `list(in:)` unchanged.
- `app/Sources/GraphicRegistry.swift` — `compile(_:library:)` from `private` to internal (reused by `GraphicTemplateLibrary`).
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+GraphicRender.swift` — `graphicContext(...)` from `private` to internal (reused by the preview).
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+GraphicBrowser.swift` (new) — `listGraphics`, `insertGraphic` handlers.
- `app/Sources/AgentCatalog+Graphics.swift` — two `tool(...)` rows after `restore_graphic`; header comment; `add_graphic_clip`'s "Insert ▸ Graphic is…" sentence updated.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer.swift` (frozen) — two handler-table rows only.
- `app/Sources/AssistantPrompt.swift` — the graphics `searchTopics` row gains both tools (F4 needs every tool exactly once).
- `app/Sources/UIMenuTable.swift` — drop `insertGraphicTemplate:` / `insertGraphicFromFile:`, add `"showGraphicBrowser:": .sheet`.
- `app/Sources/AgentCatalog.swift`, `app/Sources/AgentServer+Gate.swift` — "ninety-eight" → "one hundred" in comments.
- `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json` — the selectors and sites to match (the browser's `presentAsSheet`; From File…'s `beginSheetModal` now `reached_after` `showGraphicBrowser:`).
- `tools/proof/graphics_menu_probe.swift`, `tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py` — M2 (Insert ▸ Graphic… one item), M4/M5 (selectors), M6/M7 through the sheet; new rows below; mutants.

- `tools/proof/sheet_queue_probe.swift` — V1's door list: `insertGraphicFromFile:` and `insertGraphicTemplate:` replaced by `showGraphicBrowser:`.
- `tools/proof/op_argument_proof.py` (`PRODUCT_TOOLS = 100`), `phase9_proof.py`, `recording_proof.py`, `recording_probe.py` (`APP_STATE_TOOLS` += both) — tool counts/sets.
- `tools/proof/README.md` — the new proof's section; the count paragraph (100); `graphics_menu_proof.py`'s rows and `PROBE_MUTANTS`; `sheet_queue_probe`'s V1 list and its site table rows (`insertGraphicFromFile:`, `reportingGraphicFailure` via `insertGraphicTemplate:`) re-pathed to the sheet.

- `docs/guide/graphics.md` ("Adding a graphic": the dialog, categories, This Project; the table gains a Category column), `docs/guide/menus-and-shortcuts.md` (Insert row), `docs/guide/mcp.md` (count, two rows), `docs/manual-checks.md` (new GR-14; the "Insert ▸ Graphic ▸ X" steps of CT-8 (line 234), GR-4 (550), GR-12 (599) and GR-13 (606) re-pathed to Insert ▸ Graphic…), `CONTEXT.md` (Template: Insert ▸ Graphic…, title from `meta.name`; add **Category**), `README.md` (the "Motion graphics" highlight: the 23 built-ins browsed by category with a live preview).
- `CLAUDE.md`, `app/CLAUDE.md` — map entries for the new files and the changed roles; "ninety-eight" → "one hundred"; the app-state tool list.

## Interfaces
```swift
// GraphicCatalog.swift
struct GraphicBrowserItem: Equatable {
    enum Origin: String { case template, project }
    let name: String            // template: file stem; project: module name
    let title: String           // GraphicCatalog.title(meta:name:); a This Project duplicate gets " — <name>" (G-45 (e))
    let description: String?
    let category: String        // the module's own (meta.category, else "Other")
    let origin: Origin
    let ok: Bool                // compiled
}
struct GraphicBrowserCategory: Equatable { let name: String; let items: [GraphicBrowserItem] }
enum GraphicCatalog {
    static let thisProject = "This Project", other = "Other"
    static func category(meta: [String: Any]) -> String
    static func title(meta: [String: Any], name: String) -> String       // meta.name if non-empty string, else GraphicTemplates.title(for:)
    static func description(meta: [String: Any]) -> String?
    static func categories(templates: [GraphicBrowserItem], project: [GraphicBrowserItem]) -> [GraphicBrowserCategory]  // G-45 (d), (e)'s disambiguation
    static func categories(for document: ProjectDocument) -> [GraphicBrowserCategory]  // main only
}
final class GraphicTemplateLibrary {
    struct Entry { let template: GraphicTemplate; let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry }
    static let shared: GraphicTemplateLibrary   // GraphicTemplates.bundledDirectory, ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory
    init(directory: URL, fonts: URL)
    var entries: [Entry] { get }                 // compiled once (NSLock-memoised), first read on main
    func entry(named: String) -> Entry?
}
// GraphicPreviewPlayer.swift
final class GraphicPreviewPlayer {
    enum Subject { case module(GraphicModule, name: String, meta: [String: Any]); case failed(name: String, [GraphicDiagnostic]) }
    init(canvas: CanvasSnapshot, onFrame: @escaping (CGImage) -> Void)   // onFrame delivered on main, newest subject only
    func play(_ subject: Subject?)   // main
    func stop()                      // main; the render thread exits
}
// GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift
final class GraphicBrowserSheetController: NSViewController {
    init(document: ProjectDocument, editor: EditorViewController)
}
// identifiers: graphicbrowser.categories, .graphics, .preview, .title, .description, .message, .fromFile, .cancel, .insert
// ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift
extension ProjectDocument {
    func writeGraphicModule(from url: URL) throws -> String                       // UTF-8 check, uniqueModuleName, write, rescan; the name
    func graphicClipMaker(named name: String) throws -> (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp // meta duration/size + schema; throws "graphics/<name>.js does not compile: <msg>[ (line N)]"
}
// EditorViewController
@objc func showGraphicBrowser(_ sender: Any?)
func insertProjectGraphic(named: String, grouped: Bool) throws
static func generatedClipOps(in document: ProjectDocument, _ make: (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp) -> [ReelOp]
// AgentServer
func listGraphics(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String   // UI path: Insert ▸ Graphic…'s two lists
func insertGraphic(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String  // UI path: Insert ▸ Graphic…'s Insert
```
MCP: `list_graphics {}` → `{"categories":[{"name","graphics":[{"name","title","description"|null,"category","from":"template"|"project","ok"}]}]}`, the dialog's order exactly. `insert_graphic {name: string (required), from: "template"|"project" (required)}` → `editResult(document, "Insert Graphic", ops, ["name": <module placed>])`; unknown name refused naming it and listing that origin's names; a document with no editor/store refused with `insertGraphic`'s existing sentence. Neither in `offMainTools`; no `scope` (app-state).

## Approach
1. **Spec §11 G-45 first** (graphics.md, README row "amends G-16"): (a) a module's category is `meta.category` when a string non-empty after trimming, else "Other"; (b) every bundled template declares one of Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube, Titles & Text, and a one-line `meta.description`; (c) Data & Time: bar-chart, counter, countdown, donut-chart, gauge, line-chart, progress-bar; Screencast: arrow-highlight, callout, keyboard-keys, step-badge, window-frame; Titles & Text: chapter-card, kinetic-type, logo-reveal, lower-third, news-ticker, quote-card, title-card; Social & YouTube: end-screen, handle-tag, social-popup, subscribe-button; (d) the list: This Project first, only when the package's `graphics/` holds a module (every project module, whatever its own category), then the templates' categories by case-insensitive name, Other last; items by title case-insensitively, then name; (e) title is `meta.name`, else the stem title; a This Project item whose title equals another This Project item's (case-insensitive) is shown as "<title> — <module name>" (sheet and `list_graphics` alike); templates are now compiled (once per process, against the bundled fonts) — the menu bar still compiles nothing; (f) the door is Insert ▸ Graphic…, a sheet; Insert is G-16's act for a template, and for a This Project graphic places a clip drawn by that module with no copy; one undo step "Insert Graphic".
2. Templates' `meta` (23 files) + `template_meta.rs`; docs `Meta` keys. `cargo test --release` in `graphic/`.
3. `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift` and `generatedClipOps`, moving code out of `insertGraphic(from:grouped:)` / `addGeneratedClip` with no behaviour change; `make typecheck`.
4. `GraphicCatalog.swift`; `GraphicPreviewPlayer` — one Foundation `Thread` per player, `stackSize = GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes`; frame = ⌊elapsed × fps⌋ mod length (meta `durationInFrames`, else 5 s ceiled); ctx from `AgentServer.graphicContext` at the module's size (meta width/height, else the canvas), `props` `"{}"`, `GraphicRegistry.previewBudgetMs`; raster composited over `render_graphic`'s checker into a `CGImage`; a throw or a `.failed` subject is the error card (`LayerRenderers.errorCardText` + `paintErrorCard`); paced to fps, skipping when slow; never touches AppKit or the document off main.
5. The sheet: fixed content ~920×560; three single-column `NSTableView`s (categories ~180 pt, graphics ~240 pt) and the preview well at the canvas aspect ratio with title (bold) and description (one line, tail-truncated) under it; message label above the bottom bar; bottom bar From File… left, Cancel (Esc) and Insert (Return, default) right. Opens on the first category's first graphic. Insert disabled with no graphic selected; double-click a graphic = Insert. Insert runs in the button's event (`grouped: false`), dismisses on success, and on a throw shows the sentence word for word in the message label and stays up. From File… sets a pending flag and dismisses; the controller's `viewDidDisappear` then calls `editor.insertGraphicFromFile(nil)` (ReverseProgressSheetController.swift:75-84's pattern: a sheet just dismissed is still `attachedSheet`). `viewDidDisappear` also calls `player.stop()`, so every close (Cancel, Esc, Insert, From File…) stops the render thread. `showGraphicBrowser` presents with `presentAsSheet`; validator: `document?.graphicStore != nil`.
6. Menu, `UIMenuTable`, `inventory.json`; agent handlers, catalog rows, `AssistantPrompt` row, frozen-file wiring.

# graphic/CLAUDE.md — the graphics engine's rules

Applies to everything under `graphic/`, the crate that draws a graphic clip
(road map 10: `designs/adr/roadmap-10-graphics.md`; the full design is
`archive/roadmap-10.md` §5a). Build commands are the root
`CLAUDE.md`'s: `make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core.
The crate's record is road map 10 §10.4.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
  only. No implementation code.
- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.
- `library.rs` — `Library`: the font set (`fontdb`, from bytes, never
  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
  what resvg never reports. The generic families map to bundled faces
  (`serif` Source Serif 4, `sans-serif` Source Sans 3, `monospace` IBM Plex
  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
  nothing and is warned.
- `raster.rs` — `rasterize`, `MAX_SIDE`, the RGBA→BGRA row copy into the
  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:
  missing family, unparseable `font-family` (the scan of attributes, `style`
  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in
  a `style` attribute or sheet), unknown href, data: URL, non-image
  asset, size mismatch. The texts are load-bearing: tests match them and

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its tracks, clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests, with the serde defaults that say what an absent
  key means. The struct field names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here
  but `CanvasOutput` (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when
  `hlg`, format 23, spec §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `AudioProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`,
  `Filter`, `Reflection`, `BlendMode`, `Compressor`, `Duck`) and their
  defaults, re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every `crate::model::X` path
  holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and `TrackMatte`'s declaration
  ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry
  `hlg` (the default), `pq` or `sdr`, every other video row writes the SDR
  version, and `hlg`/`pq` are refused in an SDR project and on any other row, each in its own sentence.
- `av1_mp4.rs` · `ffi_av1.rs` — AV1 in MP4 (spec §11 CX-12, road map
  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,
  refused on any other row) are `export_table.rs`' and `export_overrides.rs`';
  `Container` is `export_container.rs`'.
- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.
- `export_preset.rs` — `Preset`, its `impl` and `fps_json`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C5's toll T1, a pure move) and re-exported there.
- `webm_ebml.rs` · `webm_layout.rs` · `webm_writer.rs` · `ffi_webm.rs` — the
  WebM an `av1_webm` or `vp9_webm` export writes (spec §11 CX-6, CX-15, CX-16: `V_VP9` with
  no CodecPrivate, BitsPerChannel 8 or 10; CX-17: `alpha_mode` on `V_VP9`, MaxBlockAdditionID
  and AlphaMode 1, `add_video_with_alpha`), the write side beside
  the importer's reader: `webm_ebml.rs` the element IDs, vints and builders
  (EBML header, Info, the TrackEntries with Colour and OpusHead, Chapters,
  SeekHead) with `webm_ebml_block.rs` the Cues and block builders and the alpha BlockGroup
  (BlockAdditions, BlockAddID 1, a ReferenceBlock on non-key blocks; C5's toll T2);
  `webm_layout.rs` `rc_webm_open`'s JSON as `WebmLayout`, each
  value checked in a sentence naming it; `webm_writer.rs` `WebmWriter`, the
  interleave (earliest head, video first on a tie), Clusters at each key and
  before 32,767 ms, Cues, the SeekHead and the Segment size patched at
  `finish`; `ffi_webm.rs` the six `rc_webm_*` exports over a
  `Mutex<WebmWriter>`. It writes the bytes it is handed and never decodes.
- `hdr10.rs` · `ffi_hdr10.rs` — an HDR10 file's peak (spec §11 HD-6,
  HD-12): the mastering-display and content-light blobs of a sample
  description, else the first sample's prefix SEI (payloads 137, 144,
  emulation-prevention bytes removed); MaxCLL first, rounded in u64,
  clamped to 10,000; `rc_hdr10_peak` its export. `av1_peak` the same for
  AV1 (HD-18): the HDR_CLL and HDR_MDCV metadata OBUs of the `av1C`'s
  config OBUs, else the first sample, luminance in 24.8 fixed point;
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak` its export. Pure, bounded reads. `rc_hdr10_still_peak`
  (HD-20) is the third export, over `hdr10_still.rs`.
- `hdr10_still.rs` — a PQ still's HDR10 peak (spec §11 HD-20, #325): a PNG's
  `cLLI`/`mDCV` chunks before the first IDAT, else a HEIF/AVIF primary item's
  `clli`/`mdcv` properties (its first `ipma`); MaxCLL first, the same rounding
  and clamp as `hdr10.rs`. Pure, every index checked against the buffer.
- `model_matte.rs` — the matte vocabulary (format version 14, spec §11 MT-1):
  `TrackMatte` (`none`, `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma`, `luma_inverted`)
  and `is_none`, re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD
  `Track.matte` stays in `model.rs`, skipped when `none` (an ordinary track
  writes no key), as `ColorAdjust`'s nine tone keys are when 0.
- `model_color.rs` — `normalise_color`, G-12's colour grammar (hex,
  `rgb()`/`rgba()`, `hsl()`/`hsla()` and the CSS named colours, from
  svgtypes' table) to lowercase `#rrggbb[aa]`; out of range is refused,
  never clamped. The stdlib's `__parseColour` implements the same grammar,
  and both suites read `graphic/tests/colours.json`. `rc_normalise_color`
  (`ffi.rs`) exports it for the Inspector's colour defaults (spec §11 G-25
  (c)), and `model_graphic.rs`'s `check_schema` refuses a `color` default
  it refuses (G-25 (a)). `color_channels` and `color_hex` (which
  `normalise_color` writes through) and `oklab_mix` are
  `actions_graphic.rs`'s blend's: `oklab_mix` is the stdlib's
  `interpolateColors` ported operation for operation (spec §11 G-40), now
  bytes/255 through `oklab_mix_unit` and ×255 rounded out; `oklab_mix_unit`
  and `oklab_mix_rgb` (0–1 floats, clamped, never rounded) are
  `actions_color.rs`'s (G-43). Three suites read `graphic/tests/oklab.json`:
  the stdlib's, `graphic_actions.rs` and `action_colours.rs`.
- `model_query.rs` — reading a project: `Project::new`, id allocation, the
  `clip`/`track`/`media`/`marker`/`nest` lookups, `clips_on`, `duration`,
  `validate` with its nesting walk, and `source_size`; and the shared
  spellings of a fresh thing: `Track::ordinary` (every flag off),
  `Source::media` (the media a source reads, exhaustive over the kinds),
  `next_track_name` ("Track N" by the count), `numbered_track` (allocated
  and named, not inserted) and `remint` (a copied clip's fresh ids: the
  clip's, then each action's). The three source-window measurements moved
  out to `source_window.rs`.
- `frame_grid.rs` — clip-time normalization shared by canvas rate changes,
  both full-paste paths and unnest. It snaps placement start, delegates the
  source-bounded duration to `source_window.rs`, clamps action spans, snaps
  present base motion/text timing through the patch snappers, and snaps a
  graphic's `in` and `length` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_resnapped` (spec §11 G-18). It does not change source positions,
  action-end payloads or audio envelopes. On a ramped clip (SR-19 (g))
  `resnap_actions` snaps the speed actions without clamping them into the
  clip (clamping would change what it reads), and `resnap_clip_times` holds
  the duration a second time over the snapped map.
- `source_window.rs` — THE source window: how much material a clip shows,
  how much lies either side of it, and the one way a source in point moves.
  `content_length_in_source` reads `speed_map.rs`'s map for a ramped clip
  (SR-10), so the one function still says how much source any clip reads.
  On a ramped clip (SR-18) the tail readers go through `time_for_source`,
  `in` moves by `source_read_by` / `source_advanced_through` (trims, roll,
  split, freeze), `front_edge_held` bisects the front edge to a frame that
  fits, and `window_of` / `overrun` (moved here from `edit_action_speed.rs`)
  are the fit test.
  **Every name here carries its UNIT**, because the readers divide by a
  clip's speed where the movers multiply by it: `content_length_in_source`,
  `last_in_point` and `last_still_time` answer in SOURCE ticks;
  `source_head_on_timeline`, `source_length_on_timeline` and
  `longest_duration_on_grid` — the bound, snapped DOWN (spec §11, #22) — in
  TIMELINE ticks. **Every site that WRITES a media clip's window reads the
  bound here, and which function it reads says what it writes** (spec §11,
  D4-2 to D4-5): `longest_duration_on_grid_of` is the bound from the pieces,
  with the clip's `start` among them, because a DURATION is measured from 0
  and an END from the clip's own start and the two are not the same number;
  `latest_end_on_grid` and `earliest_start_on_grid` are the timeline
  POSITIONS `trim_end` / `roll` and `trim_start` / `roll` /
  `head_handle_frames` clamp to (positions, so not a `SourceBound`);
  `duration_resnapped` is what every RE-SNAP of a media duration writes
  (`resnap`, `paste` twice, `unnest`, `relink_media`'s hold to a shorter file)
  and `duration_at_speed` what
  `set_speed` writes. No local clamp anywhere else. A measurement is a
  `SourceBound` and not an `Option`,
  because `None` meant "unbounded, apply no clamp" to a trim and "no handle
  at all" to a transition: the three arms are `Unbounded` (a source with no
  window), `Unmeasured` (a media window that exists and cannot be measured)
  and `Timeline`, and a caller picks what `Unmeasured` means to it BY NAME,
  `or_unbounded` or `or_empty`. `in_advanced` / `source_advanced` is the one
  `round(Δ × speed)` mover the six placement sites used to write out. Cut
  out of `model_query.rs` by road map 7 §10's phase A.
- `time.rs` — `Ticks`, `TIMESCALE`, `Fps`, frame snapping, timecode
  format/parse (non-drop `HH:MM:SS:FF` and `HH:MM:SS.mmm`). Snapping keeps
  frame indices wide through directional adjustment and saturates only at the
  public tick/index result. `frames_in` (whole grid frames in a length),
  `frames_back` (the grid position k frames before the frame nearest a
  position) and `frames_within` (the most whole frames back from a position
  that stay within a span), `frames_between` (the whole grid frames between
  two positions) and `one_frame` (the grid's own first frame, which
  `Project::frame` is at every rate, 1/30 s only at a degenerate rate; spec
  §11 #174) count on the canvas's own grid at a rate the
  timescale does not divide (spec §11 #42).
- `time_bounds.rs` — the single structural-time admission checker and
  `MAX_STORED_TICKS`: ±9,000,000,000,000,000 for stored media, markers,
  clips, source positions and actions, including clip/action endpoints in
  i128. `Project::validate` and `format::write` both call it; vocabulary
  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).
- `edit.rs` — the op enum, `parse` and `apply`. **Its module doc IS the op
  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders, `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s
  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).
- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-two op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (nineteen kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.
- `scope.rs` — editing INSIDE a nest: the envelope's `scope` key. Builds a
  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.
- `edit_graphic.rs` — `add_graphic_clip` and `set_graphic`: every argument
  checked through `model_graphic.rs` BEFORE `edit_clip.rs`'s
  `add_described_clip` (`pub(crate)`, with `Described`) places the clip, so
  the op table's bound probe reaches the side check on any project;
  `set_graphic`'s patch reader takes `name`, `width`, `height`, `length`,
  `props` and refuses `in` by name. With a `schema`, a `null` for a prop
  an action on the clip names stores the schema's default (G-34 (d)).
- `edit_clip.rs` — clip construction and placement callers: `add_clip`, move,
  duplicate, delete, join, `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized
  footage and honours `canvas.fit_new_clips`; Fill is a REQUIREMENT, ignores
  it, scales up as readily as down and clamps to `SCALE_MAX`). `whole_media_length`,
  `edit_clip_timing.rs`'s `trim_end` and `set_speed` hold a media clip's window INSIDE its file, each
  through `source_window.rs`'s one bound, so
  `in + duration × speed ≤ media.duration` and the plan's segment rate is
  exactly the clip's speed (spec §11, #22 and D4-2 to D4-5); the other
  writers are `edit_canvas.rs`'s `resnap`, `edit_paste.rs`'s two loops,
  `edit_nest.rs`'s `unnest` and `edit_background.rs`'s timed plate. Over
  the cap, known debt (below).
- `edit_clip_timing.rs` — `trim_start`, `trim_end`, `rate_stretch`, `set_speed`,
  their speed bounds and clip-relative action rescaling; `AUDIO_SPEED_MAX`
  (×12, spec §11 #190) and `speed_limits`, which `rc_speed_limits` publishes;
  `set_speed` takes a `rate` or a `duration` (Fit to duration), exactly one.
  On a ramped clip (SR-19 (a), (b)) both rate edits scale the WHOLE profile
  by one factor (`profile_factors`, None on every constant clip):
  `scaled_profile` scales the base, every end rate and every speed span
  (`scaled_span`, snapped, never clamped, which `rescale_actions` also uses),
  writes an unclamped rate as asked, holds the window, then re-clamps the
  other actions into the held duration through `resnap_actions`.
  `trim_start` advances a graphic's `in` through `graphic_advanced` (no speed,
  no head bound, saturating at 0); `trim_end` leaves `length` alone.
- `edit_detach.rs` — `detach_audio` and `set_enabled`, a clip's video and
  audio halves; a pure move out of `edit_clip.rs` (grading L3).
- `edit_commit.rs` — the placement commit protocol: replacements preserve
  caller order and check old tracks before destination tracks; additions
  check caller-allocated candidates against the input project; both write
  one draft and call `finish_placement`, which mints gained transitions on
  exactly the chosen tracks before `finish`. `finish` remains equality first,
  validation second, and does not itself refuse. `Clip::placed` is the one
  literal of a newly placed clip (each placing site overrides it by struct
  update); `add_tracks_behind` and `Landing` are unnest's and paste's shared
  landing: deficit tracks inserted behind, fallbacks pushed in front, the
  touched tracks in first-seen order for `finish_placement`.
- `edit_split.rs` — `split_clip` and what the SECOND clip inherits: base
  props from the evaluation at the cut, unfinished actions rebased, a
  straddled one narrowed, presets and motion halves anchored to the two
  ends. Every splitter in the crate routes here, so a rule stated once is a
  rule they all obey. A free function over `&mut Project` because it is
  called mid-edit on a clone the caller is still assembling.
  A graphic's second half gets `in + cut` through `recipe_graphic.rs`'s
  `graphic_advanced`, and BOTH halves' `length` are pinned to the ORIGINAL's
  `effective_length` (G-9), so every splitter obeys it, and its `props` the
  evaluated ones, a straddled action's first half ending at them (G-34).
- `edit_props.rs` — the five patches (`set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text`,
  `set_shape`, `set_clip`), `Project::settle_video` (the one chain that
  makes a video group storable — empty motion → null, `check_video`,
  identity curves dropped, `check_blend` / `check_adjustment_video` /
  `check_qualifier_clip` / `check_look_media`, `snap_motion` — run by
  `set_video` and by every pasted video group) and
  `normalise_and_check_group` beside it (`settle_video` for a video group,
  the range check for the other three) (the one NORMALISATION a copied
  group needs first: a clipboard payload is a third door for a `Motion`, and
  an empty one has two spellings; only the file reader does not normalise;
  the copied group is checked before its present video/text timing is
  snapped), and `normalise_and_check_pasted`, which runs it over every group
  of every clip `paste` lands — nested ones in a second pass, once every
  copy is in — naming the PAYLOAD's clip id (`pasted clip N: …`, issue #62),
  `check_blend`, the one check about a CLIP rather than a value (a nest clip
  cannot blend), and `snap_motion` / `snap_animation`, which put the ticks a
  patch or checked copied group carries on the frame grid AFTER the range
  check, so a refusal names what the caller sent. What a patch may CARRY is
  `patch.rs`'s and nothing here restates it.
- `patch.rs` — reading a caller-authored patch, cut out of `edit_props.rs`
  under the size rule: `Group` — the four PATCH groups; `paste_attributes` takes these four and
  `graphic` as `edit_paste_attributes.rs`'s `PasteGroup`, and a patch has no
  fifth group — and its per-group template, `check_keys` (the
  walk of keys and JSON kinds, array indices in the path) and `merge_group`
  (the one read of a group patch — the walk, the deep merge and the
  path-tracking deserialise — the new text and shape clips' patches
  included), so every refusal names the path, indices included, and the
  value. `check_group_patch` is the same walk and read for a group that is
  NOT being merged into a stored one (an action's end state), and
  `unknown_key` is that refusal's one spelling. A patch merges key by key at
  every depth, an array replaces it

`LATEST_VERSION`) and `negotiate` (the requested one when supported, else
  the newest), moved out of `agent.rs` by road map 14's MC3 so ONE list
  serves two readers: `agent.rs`'s `initialize` and `mcp-proxy/`, which
  includes this file by `#[path]`. It therefore uses `std` alone and names
  nothing of this crate (no `use crate::…`).
- `ffi.rs` / `ffi_edit.rs` / `ffi_query.rs` / `ffi_agent.rs` — thin shims
  only; shared plumbing lives in `ffi_util.rs`, never copy-pasted.
  `ffi_query.rs`'s rule: a query never allocates a handle and has no
  `err_out`, which is why `rc_project_scoped` lives in `ffi.rs`.
  `rc_speed_limits` is its answer for the speed range and the audio ceiling;
  `rc_project_source_map` (`ffi_query.rs`, SR-20) a clip's source map;
  `rc_normalise_color` (`ffi.rs`) is the colour grammar's (G-25).
  `ffi_agent.rs` has one slot, one listener per process: `SOCKET`
  (`rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`; MC4 deleted the TCP pair and its
  slot), whose `AgentConfig` is built by `host_config`, one catalog
  through one handler.
- `container.rs` · `container_header.rs` · `container_blocks.rs` ·
  `container_codec.rs` · `container_timing.rs` · `container_vorbis.rs` ·
  `container_vorbis_setup.rs` · `ffi_container.rs` — a WebM
  or Matroska file being imported, read as an INDEX (spec §11 #216-R),
  read-only, bounds-checked, no input may panic: `container_header.rs` the
  EBML reading and the header before the first Cluster (a CodecPrivate over
  1 MiB refused by name); `container_blocks.rs` the Cluster walk
  (unknown-size Clusters end at the next level-1 element, three lacings,
  payloads skipped, a truncated tail ends the index); `container_codec.rs`
  codec ID → fourcc, the synthesised `vpcC`, the AAC ES_Descriptor, Opus TOC
  counts; `container_timing.rs` raw and grid-snapped video times, decode
  times by the largest reorder, audio in samples less CodecDelay,
  laced-frame times, `required_bytes`, and Vorbis's lead (the first packet's
  count); `container_vorbis.rs` the three Vorbis headers walked to the mode
  table, each packet's count by the overlap rule (spec §11 #228-V), with
  `container_vorbis_setup.rs` the setup header's walk (codebooks, floors,
  residues, mappings, modes); `container.rs` the first video and
  audio track and `describe`/`retime`/`sample_count`/`sample`;
  `ffi_container.rs` the six `rc_container_*` exports. The Colour
  element's MaxCLL, MaxFALL and MasteringMetadata are read too (HD-18):
  `container_codec.rs` writes them as the `mdcv`/`clli` blobs (and reads them
  back, `mastering_from_mdcv` and `light_from_clli`, for the WebM writer) and
  `describe` publishes `mdcv_hex`, `clli_hex`, `transfer`, `primaries`,
  `matrix` and `stream_matrix` (the first VP9 keyframe's `color_space` as a matrix code,
  from `vpcc`; spec §11 CX-16 (10)); the app writes the blobs and the PQ label only for transfer 16. The only payload read
  is the first VP9 keyframe's header, each Opus packet's TOC and each Vorbis
  packet's first byte.
- `ffi_graphic.rs` — the eleven `rc_graphic_*` exports (road map 10 §5e; the
  eleventh `rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39: set the decoded-image cache's
  limit, answer its bytes; two re-exported from `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`
  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;

content.content:
seam is named.
- `ReelCore.swift`: the typed patches moved to `TypedPatches.swift` in issue batch B73 (#216), a
  pure move gated alone before `ReelContainer` landed; no further seam is named. The `dictionary`
  extensions went to `OpDictionaries.swift` in issue batch B52b (#190), the media helpers earlier
  to `MediaDescriptor.swift`. Road map 14's MC2 made the same `dictionary` move on its branch
  (`PropsDictionaries.swift`) before adding `ReelAgentSocket`; the merge into main kept
  `OpDictionaries.swift`, whose code is identical (only its
  `import` and the doc comment's file name differ). It stays the only file that calls
  `rc_*`. The HDR road map's H-1 paid a toll before `ReelHDR10` (#281) landed: lines 411–583 at
  `dcd08f3` — `ExportPreset`, `ExportSettings`, `ExportSize` and their docs, none naming an `rc_*`
  symbol but in a doc comment — went whole to `ExportValues.swift` under `import AppKit` and a
  three-line doc, a pure move gated alone; nothing widened (no member was `private` to the file).
  `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 989 before, 815 after; `ExportValues.swift` is 178. The next
  seam: the graphics engine's value types (`GraphicDiagnostic`, `GraphicFailure`,
  `GraphicRaster`, under `// MARK: - Graphics`) and `SpeedLimits` out to a values file, each
  naming no `rc_*` symbol; `takeDiagnostics` stays, since it frees through `takeString`.
  Clean-up batch 2 paid that seam before `ReelHDR10.av1Peak` (#316, spec §11 HD-18) landed:
  `SpeedLimits` and `GraphicDiagnostic`, `GraphicFailure` and `GraphicRaster` with their docs
  went whole to `CoreValues.swift` under `import Foundation` and a three-line doc, a pure move
  gated alone (`04-toll.patch`); `takeDiagnostics`, `ReelSpeed` and the `// MARK:` lines
  stayed, and nothing widened. `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 842 before, 800 after;
  `CoreValues.swift` is 47. The next seam: `ReelCoreError` and the `Fps.ffiPair` extension
  (lines 41–78 less the three private string helpers) out to `CoreValues.swift`, neither
  calling an `rc_*` symbol. #127 G6 phase 5 paid that seam (toll T2) before
  `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (spec §11 G-39) landed: `ReelCoreError` (lines 41–45) and
  `extension Fps { var ffiPair }` (lines 67–76) with their docs went whole to the head of
  `CoreValues.swift`, whose doc gained a clause, and the header gained its payment sentence; a
  pure move gated alone, nothing widened (neither was `private`), the three private string
  helpers stayed. `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 817 before, 803 after; `CoreValues.swift`
  is 65. The next seam: the parsing halves of `ReelProject.snapCandidates(excluding:)` (the
  JSON-to-`Set<Ticks>` absorb) and `clipState(_:at:)` (the JSON object read) as static helpers
  in a values file, the `rc_*` calls staying here. Clean-up 3 batch B paid that seam (toll T1)
  before `ReelHDR10.stillPeak(file:)` (#325, spec §11 HD-20) landed: `enum CoreJSON` in
  `CoreValues.swift` took `value(_:)` (the JSON object read, nil for a nil or unreadable string)
  and `snapTicks(_:)` (the object-of-arrays or one-array absorb, merged, de-duplicated and
  sorted); `clipState` and `snapCandidates` call them, their `rc_*` calls and `jsonArray`
  staying, and the header gained its payment sentence. A pure move gated alone, nothing widened.
  `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 810 before, 795 after; `CoreValues.swift` is 94. The next
  seam: the private `jsonArray` above `ReelProject` (it names no `rc_*` symbol) to `CoreJSON`,
  widened to internal. Speed ramps SR4-0 paid a different seam before `rc_project_source_map`'s
  wrapper (#111, spec §11 SR-20) landed: `ReelTime.perSecond`, `ticks(seconds:)` and
  `seconds(_:)` went whole to an `extension ReelTime` in `CoreValues.swift`, and the
  JSON-reading half of `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` to `ReelOpSchema.table(from:)`, the
  `rc_op_schemas()` call staying; a pure move gated alone, nothing widened. `wc -l
  app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 803 before, 774 after; `CoreValues.swift` is 116. The next seam is
  still `jsonArray`.
  Codec-export C1 paid it (toll T2) before `ReelAV1` (`rc_av1_*`, spec §11 CX-12 (4)) landed:
  `jsonArray` went whole to `CoreJSON.array` in `CoreValues.swift` (internal where it was
  `private`; its two callers, `snapCandidates(excluding:)` and `ReelSnap.resolve`, renamed),
  a pure move gated alone by `make typecheck`. `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift`: 789 before, 782
  after; `CoreValues.swift` 138 → 147. `ReelAV1` then took ReelCore to 859, over the cap.
  C1's fix pass paid that back before merge in two pure moves, each gated alone by `make
  typecheck` (exit 0, the four baseline warnings): first `ReelAV1.Config` (with its hex decoder)
  and `ReelAV1.Color` went whole to an `extension ReelAV1` in `CoreValues.swift` (859 → 823;
  `CoreValues.swift` 147 → 187); then the `rc_*`-free halves of five members went there too —
  `ReelExport.settings`' overrides encoding as `CoreJSON.overrides(_:)`, `takeDiagnostics`'
  decode as `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`, `GraphicLibrary.rasterize`'s side refusal as

  one, and a looping preview; a template declares its category and a
  one-line description** (owner, 2026-10-29: a graphic browser in place of

  (b) **Every bundled template declares one** of Data & Time,
  Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text, and a one-line
  `meta.description` of at most 120 characters, held by
  `graphic/tests/template_meta.rs` to (c)'s table.
  (c) **The table.** Data & Time: bar-chart, counter, countdown,
  donut-chart, gauge, line-chart, progress-bar. Screencast:
  arrow-highlight, callout, keyboard-keys, step-badge, window-frame.
  Titles & Text: chapter-card, kinetic-type, logo-reveal, lower-third,
  news-ticker, quote-card, title-card. Social & YouTube: end-screen,
  handle-tag, social-popup, subscribe-button.
  (d) **The list.** This Project first, and only when the package's
  `graphics/` holds a module: every project module, whatever its own
  category. Then the templates' categories by case-insensitive name, Other
  last. Within a category the graphics go by title case-insensitively,
  then by name. `list_graphics` answers the same order.

  stem's title (`lower-third` → "Lower Third"). A This Project graphic whose
  title equals another This Project graphic's, case-insensitively, is shown
  as "<title> — <module name>", in the dialog and in `list_graphics` alike,
  so two copies of one template can be told apart. The templates are now
  COMPILED to read their `meta`, once per process, against the bundled
  fonts; the menu bar still compiles nothing (chrome probes instantiate
  `AppDelegate()`).

  File… item are gone; From File… is the sheet's bottom-left button, and
  its open panel follows once the sheet is down). Insert is G-16's act for
  a template: the module written under a free name (G-16 (b)), then one
  clip. For a This Project graphic it places a clip drawn by that module

  (G-16 (c)'s "was written but" is gone, since a This Project graphic was
  not written). The agent's mirror is `list_graphics` and
  `insert_graphic {name, from}`.

"""The capture spike's Q2(c) inventory: which menu items reach a sheet, a
modal run loop, or neither — and the checks that hold `inventory.json` to
the tree (road map 11, V1).

`inventory.json` is READ BY HAND, site first: every line the grep below
finds is traced to the menu selectors that reach it, synchronously
(`reached_from`: the action method reaches the site before it returns) or
later (`reached_after`: from a sheet or panel completion, an async hop or an
AppKit delegate callback, with the `via` line and the `gate` that must hold).
Every other live selector is read to `none`, `window` or `framework`.
The grep counts the APP-MODAL `presentError(` (road map 11's V2b) — the
`presentError(_:)` / `NSApp.presentError(_:)` that runs a modal loop — and
not the sheet form `presentError(_:modalFor:…)`, which is not modal.

  I1  every leaf of `buildMainMenu()` (the probe's `menu` mode) has its
      selector in `selectors`, and every row there names a live selector;
  I2  the grep's sites and `sites` are one-to-one, each line holding its token
      and lying in its entry's `func`; a site is FOUND BY ITS TOKEN AND ITS
      ENCLOSING FUNCTION, not its line (#166, #168): `resolve` pairs the
      inventory's sites with the grep's per (file, token, func) — `func` the
      nearest `func NAME` or `init(` declaration at or above the line — in
      line order, whenever the two counts agree, so a line added above a
      site moves its pin instead of failing it; where they disagree each pin
      stands as written. A site removed and another added in one file and
      token no longer balance unless both are in one function, so a swap
      across functions is reported (K4);
  I3  every citation is checked for content (#168). A citation is a SITE ref,
      `app/Sources/<F>.swift:<N>` naming a key of `sites` (read at its
      resolved line), or an ANCHORED ref, ``app/Sources/<F>.swift `<anchor>` ``,
      whose anchor is a piece of the line meant and occurs exactly once in
      `<F>`. Each `code` item is exactly one citation; `note`, `via`, `gate`
      and `other_caller` hold citations in prose; any other `<F>.swift:<N>`
      is a problem, as is a line citation that is not a site, an anchor
      missing or not unique, and a `reached_after` whose `via` cites nothing.
      A `modal` selector cites a line holding a loop token, a `sheet` one a
      sheet token; every `reached_from` / `reached_after` selector names a
      row; a selector in the `reached_from` of a `runModal` or loop-token
      site is `modal` (`reached_after` never forces a verdict);
  I4  the checker over a copy missing one selector and one site reports
      exactly those two (the first selector no site references, and the
      first site no citation names by its line).

`python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.py --check` is a line of
`make test`: no app, no probe, no build, in a fresh `work/inventory_check/`.

      `v2_menu.py`'s H1); its detail lists the pins found at another line;

      of every file that holds a site or is cited by an anchor has no I2 or
      I3 problem;
  K3  CONTROL: a fresh copy, the inventory's site keys first rewritten
      through `resolve`, then the line of the first rewritten site blanked:
      the checker reports exactly that site under I2;
  K4  CONTROL: a fresh copy, the keys rewritten, the first site's line
      blanked and `func b13Swap() { <that line> }` appended as the file's
      last line — a swap in one file and token: I2 reports exactly that site
      (its line does not hold its token) and the appended line (a grep site
      missing from the inventory);
  K5  CONTROL: the first anchored `code` citation (selectors sorted) with an
      invisible U+2063 appended to its anchor: `check` reports exactly that

```json screen
{

  "project": "demo",

  "expect": [{"capture": "sheet", "visible_text": "Insert Graphic"}]
}
```

The Graphic dialog (Insert ▸ Graphic…, spec §11 G-45) is where a person
picks a motion graphic to put on the timeline. The demo project holds one
graphic of its own, `lower-third`, so the dialog opens on This Project.

Under the title "Insert Graphic" are three panes side by side. On the left, a
bordered list of categories: "This Project" (selected, a grey row), then the
bundled templates' four, "Data & Time", "Screencast", "Social & YouTube" and
"Titles & Text". In the middle, a wider bordered list of the chosen
category's graphics by name — here the one, "Lower third", selected. On the
right, the preview: the chosen graphic playing over a grey checkerboard, at
the canvas's shape (16:9 for the demo), looping; under it the graphic's name
in bold and its one-line description in grey, cut short with "…" if it is
longer than the preview is wide. The capture catches whichever frame of the
loop was showing; early in Lower third's loop the bar may not have slid in
yet.

A line under the panes is empty until an Insert is refused; then it holds
the reason, word for word ("graphics/<name>.js does not compile: …"), and
the dialog stays open. That is not captured here.

Bottom left, "From File…", a square outlined button: it closes the dialog
and asks for a `.js` file instead. Bottom right, "Cancel" (Esc) and a blue
"Insert" (Return; a double-click on a graphic does the same). Insert is
greyed when no graphic is chosen.

In the light capture the sheet is white with black text, the lists white
with a thin grey border and the selected rows light grey. In the dark capture
the sheet is near-black with white text, the lists near-black with a thin
grey border and the selected rows dark grey; the checkerboard is the same
grey in both.
digit, and are at most 63 characters (`lower-third`, `title-2`).

Graphics draw only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the ones you add
to the project (see [Fonts and pictures](#fonts-and-pictures)), never with
the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere.

## Adding a graphic

**Insert ▸ Graphic…** opens the Graphic dialog. On the left are the
categories: **This Project** first, when the project's `graphics/` folder
holds a module (every module in it, whatever its own category), then the
bundled templates' categories, in alphabetical order. In the middle are the
chosen category's graphics, by name. On the right a preview plays the chosen
graphic over a checkerboard, looping, at the project's canvas shape, with its
name and a one-line description under it. A module that doesn't compile is
listed in grey and its preview is the red error card.

The dialog opens on the first category's first graphic. **Insert** (Return,
or a double-click on a graphic) adds the chosen graphic; **Cancel** (Esc)
closes the dialog; **From File…** closes it and asks for a `.js` module to
copy into the project instead.

A module of your own goes into a category by giving its `meta` a `category`
(and a `description` for the line under the preview); one without a category
is listed under **Other**, last (see the [graphics reference](../graphics-api.md)).

The bundled templates:

| Template | Category | What you get | Default length |
|---|---|---|---|
| Arrow highlight | Screencast | A rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail | 90 frames |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Spec §11 G-45, phase 1 of the graphic browser — `list_graphics`,
`insert_graphic`, and Insert ▸ Graphic…'s sheet as the dev tools see it —
against the built app.

    python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py [--app PATH]
    python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py --mutant list-templates-only

**The instances.** The built app (`proof_app`'s choice), launched in a
scratch home (`CFFIXED_USER_HOME=tools/proof/work/graphic-browser/home`,
`graphics_menu_proof.py`'s launch) on a scratch socket, stopped by PID:
once with `-RCDevAppearance light` for every row, then once with
`-RCDevAppearance dark` for U1's dark capture. Nothing persisting is
performed, no sheet is confirmed. At the start and at exit everything in
`work/graphic-browser/` but the last logs is removed.

**The fixture.** `new_project` at `work/graphic-browser/GB.framejob`, saved —
a package with no module.

S0  with the instance listening, `<home>/Library/Application Support` is a
    directory (the scratch home took). When it fails no tool is called.
L1  `list_graphics` on GB: no This Project; the categories are exactly Data
    & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube, Titles & Text, each holding G-45
    (c)'s templates, ordered by title case-insensitively then name; every
    graphic is `from: template`, `ok: true`, its `category` its section's,
    its `title` the file's `meta.name`, its `description` a non-empty
    string;
I1  `insert_graphic {name: lower-third, from: template}` answers ok and
    `name: lower-third`; `graphics/lower-third.js` is byte-equal to
    `graphic/tests/graphics/lower-third.js`; one clip more, drawn by
    lower-third;
L2  `list_graphics` again: This Project first, holding exactly lower-third,
    titled "Lower third", `from: project`, category Titles & Text; then L1's
    four;
I2  `insert_graphic {name: lower-third, from: project}`: ok, `name:
    lower-third`, one clip more drawn by lower-third, and the package's
    `graphics/*.js` unchanged (no copy);
I3  `write_graphic broken` (a module that does not compile), then
    `insert_graphic {name: broken, from: project}`: refused with
    "graphics/broken.js does not compile: …", no clip added;
I4  `insert_graphic {name: nope}` from template is refused naming "nope" and
    listing lower-third among the templates; from project, naming "nope" and
    listing "broken, lower-third";
I5  `insert_graphic {name: lower-third, from: file}` is refused with "from
    must be template or project (got \\"file\\")"; and one with no `from` is
    refused naming `from`;
U1  (light, then dark on its own instance) `perform_menu_item {path:
    ["Insert", "Graphic…"]}` answers a non-null `sheet`; `snapshot_ui
    {window: sheet}` writes a non-empty PNG and a layout dump holding the
    nine identifiers `graphicbrowser.categories`, `.graphics`, `.preview`,
    `.title`, `.description`, `.message`, `.fromFile`, `.cancel`, `.insert`,

- **Answer:** for each template that fails, its name, the project (1080p, 1080×1920 or 1080×1080) and what is wrong: a jerky move, text you cannot read, or something past the outer rectangle.
- **Source:** owner 2026-10-29 (spec §11 G-44); `graphic/tests/templates.rs` measures that nothing outside title-safe moves at every fifth frame and that no frame warns, and that the last frame is bare, with defaults, every `enum` combination and every text property long, not how the motion looks.

**GR-14 — The Graphic dialog looks right and plays**
- **Setup:** a 1920×1080 project with one module of your own in its `graphics/` (e.g. write one with the assistant), and a 1080×1920 project with none.
- **Do:** In each project, Insert ▸ Graphic…. Click each category in turn and each graphic in it, watching the preview loop a few times. Use the arrow keys in the graphics list; press Esc; open it again and press Return; open it again and double-click a graphic; open it again and press From File…, then cancel the panel. Repeat in the other appearance.
- **Expect:** the dialog opens on the first category's first graphic (This Project in the first project, Data & Time in the second); every graphic's preview plays smoothly at the canvas's shape (wide in the first project, tall in the second) and loops back to its start; each description reads whole on one line under the title; Esc closes it with nothing added; Return and the double-click each add the chosen graphic at the playhead and close it; From File… closes it and shows the open panel straight after.
- **Answer:** for each graphic whose preview stutters, does not loop or has the wrong shape, its name and project; any description cut short (its name); Esc, Return, double-click and From File… each as expected, yes or no; anything wrong in the other appearance.
- **Source:** spec §11 G-45; `tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py` (M24–M32) and `tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py` measure the lists, the acts, the preview's first frame and the thread, not how the loop looks or how the keys feel.

## Mattes

**MAT-1 — A matte plays**
577:- **Setup:** Low Power Mode off — `pmset -g | grep powermode` reads 0 before and after the run (if it does not, skip this check and note it). View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full. Activity Monitor open on Frame Job's memory. Background render off in Settings ▸ Playback (spec §11 G-38), so no frame is drawn ahead while the window waits; tick it again after GR-10.
583:**GR-10 — A replay plays from memory, and the memory is given back**
590:**GR-11 — Background render draws while Frame Job is left alone, and stops when you touch it**
597:**GR-12 — A dark gradient graphic shows no rings and no visible grain**
604:**GR-13 — The bundled templates look and move right**
611:**GR-14 — The Graphic dialog looks right and plays**
724:- **Source:** grading-2's G2-1 (spec §11 GR-10) and grading-4's T4-1 (GR-26, GR-31); `tools/proof/scopes_proof.py` measures the bins, counts, timings and layout on synthetic fixtures (T1 the GPU time on a flat saturated colour), not how the scopes read on footage or whether the slide plays smoothly.
729:- **Source:** grading-2's G2-2 (spec §11 GR-11); `tools/proof/wheels_proof.py` measures the formulas on a grey card and ramp, export parity and the gesture's arithmetic, not how a grade looks on footage.
734:- **Source:** grading-2's G2-3 (spec §11 GR-12) and grading-4's T4-2 (GR-32) and T4-3 (GR-34); `tools/proof/curves_proof.py` measures the curve on a grey card and ramp, the hue curves on a synthetic hue sweep (HSV-hue change and luma), export parity and the editor's gestures, not how a curve looks on footage.
738:- **Expect:** the pick turns hue and saturation on around the skin; Show Selection shows the face white and greys and dark noise black (the chroma and near-black guards), the "Selection" tag beside the preview; the softness widens the edge smoothly with no hard ring; only the face warms, and the background and greys stay as they were; selecting a media clip turns Show Selection off and Esc leaves a pick; each strip drag and each pick undoes in one step (Hue, Saturation, Luma, Qualifier); the export is the graded picture, never the selection; the strips, knobs, squares and fields read clearly in both appearances at every width, and playback stays smooth. If the guards pick dark noise or drop real skin, the first numbers in spec §11 GR-13 are what to retune. (T4-4) Blur melts the speckle into a smooth grey edge without growing the selection onto the background, the same at Full and Half; the blur undoes in one step named Qualifier Blur and Reset sets it to 0 %; with the blur on, 4K playback stays smooth (no dropped frames you can see); if 100 % is too little or too much on real footage, the 24 px of spec §11 GR-35 is the number to retune.

# Spec: the Graphic dialog, phase 2 of 2 — Export… and the `.fjgraphic` package

## Goal
The Graphic dialog gains **Export…** at its far left, which writes the chosen graphic as a `.fjgraphic` zip holding a manifest, the module and only the project fonts and assets that the graphics engine saw it draw or measure with (never a bundled font). `export_graphic` mirrors it for agents and is ask-first in the assistant.

## Files
- `graphic/src/library.rs` — `Usage`, `Library::usage()`. `new()` loads each blob with `load_font_source` and keeps a face-ID → blob-index map. A `Mutex<UsageSet>` is filled by `options()`'s `select_font`, a wrapped `default_fallback_selector`, and `resolve_string` (only when the asset is drawable, i.e. `image_kind` is `Some`).
- `graphic/src/lib.rs` — re-export `Usage`.
- `graphic/tests/usage.rs` (new) — the usage oracles (Approach 2).
- `core/src/ffi_graphic.rs` — `rc_graphic_library_usage`; the doc's count goes from eleven to twelve.
- `core/src/graphic_package.rs` (new) — the package spec parse and checks, the manifest, the stored zip, CRC-32 and the file write. Names no `graphic` item.
- `core/src/ffi_graphic_package.rs` (new) — `rc_graphic_package_write`, through `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op` and `read_cstr`/`read_bytes`.
- `core/src/lib.rs` — `mod graphic_package;` and `pub mod ffi_graphic_package;`.
- `core/Cargo.toml` — `sha2 = "0.10"` moves from dev-dependencies to dependencies, with a comment (the manifest's checksums; already in the lock through `graphic`).
- `core/include/framejob_core.h` — the two declarations, with their contracts.
- `core/tests/graphic_package.rs` (new) — the archive oracles and the refusals (Approach 3).
- `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` — usage through the FFI: a fresh library, one `rc_graphic_rasterize` drawing Anton, then usage = `{"fonts":[<Anton's index>],"assets":[]}`; NULL → NULL.
- `core/tests/model_tests.rs` — the null sweep covers both new exports.
- `app/Sources/CoreValues.swift` — **toll first** (Approach 4): `withByteBuffer`. Also `GraphicUsage` with `decoded(_:)`.
- `app/Sources/ReelCore.swift` — the toll's call sites, `GraphicLibrary.usage()` and `enum ReelGraphicPackage`. It must end at ≤ 788 lines (its count today).
- `app/Sources/GraphicStore.swift` — `static func bundledFontURLs(in:)` and `makeIndexedLibrary()`; `makeLibrary()` becomes `try makeIndexedLibrary().library` (behaviour unchanged).
- `app/Sources/GraphicPackage.swift` (new, ≤ 400 lines) — `GraphicPackage`, `GraphicPackageJob`, `GraphicPackageResult`.
- `app/Sources/GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift` — the Export… button, the save panel, the export thread, the message line. Header comment updated.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+GraphicBrowser.swift` — `exportGraphic`. `insertGraphic`'s name/origin resolution is factored into `browserGraphic(name:from:document:)`, shared by both handlers with the same sentences.
- `app/Sources/AgentCatalog+Graphics.swift` — an `export_graphic` row after `insert_graphic`.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer.swift` (frozen; wiring only) — one handler row. `"export_graphic",` is appended to `productOffMainTools`' LAST line, after `"get_transcript",`, because `agent_open_proof.py`'s `open-on-main` anchor is the line above it. ```c

```c
 * the library. NULL only for NULL. */
char *rc_graphic_library_usage(const RcGraphicLibrary *lib);
/* Writes the .fjgraphic at `path` (created or truncated). package_json: {"module","title",
 * "category","description":string|null,"app_version","files":[{"path","size"}…]}; `data` is the
 * files' bytes concatenated in that order. False with a lowercase sentence through err_out. */
```

- **The checks in `rc_graphic_package_write`** (each refused naming its value):
  - `module` must pass `model_graphic::check_name`.
  - `title`, `category` and `app_version` must be strings; `description` is a string or null.
  - The first file is exactly `<module>.js`. Every other file is `fonts/<n>` or `assets/<n>`, where `<n>` is non-empty, at most 255 bytes, does not start with `.`, and has no `/`, `\`, `:` or control character.
  - No path appears twice.
  - The sizes sum to `len`.
  - The archive is at most `u32::MAX` bytes (no Zip64).
  - The create and the write report I/O failures.
- **The archive:**
  - Method 0 (stored), version needed 10, made by Unix 2.0 (`0x031E`), flag bit 11 (UTF-8).
  - DOS time 0 and date `0x0021` (1980-01-01), so two writes of the same input are byte-identical. No extra fields and no directory entries; external attributes `0o100644 << 16`.
  - Entries in order: `manifest.json`, then the files as given. A central directory and an EOCD follow.
- **`manifest.json`** is pretty-printed JSON with a trailing newline, keys in this order: `{"fjgraphic": 1, "module", "title", "category", "description", "app_version", "files": [{"path", "size", "sha256"}…]}`. `sha256` is 64 lowercase hex characters. The manifest does not list itself.
